newsitem.title: USA: Senate confirms first postwar U.S. envoy to Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Senate confirms first postwar U.S. envoy to Vietnam.

text.p: The U.S. Senate on Thursday confirmed former Vietnam prisoner of war Douglas "Pete" Peterson as the first postwar U.S. ambassador in Hanoi.
The long-delayed approval of the nomination came after a brief debate and without a recorded vote.
Peterson served as an Air Force pilot in Vietnam and was a prisoner of war there for more than six years. He later became a businessman and a Democratic congressman from Florida.

Hailing his confirmation, Sen. John Kerry, a Massachusetts Democrat and Vietnam veteran, said Peterson would help to bridge the gap that remained and build a normal relationship between the two former foes.

Peterson's nomination had been held up first by a legal technicality and then by Republican Sen. Bob Smith of New Hampshire, who charged that Vietnamese cooperation with efforts to account for Americans missing in action in Vietnam was inadequate.

More recently Smith had held the nomination hostage to efforts to get former Commerce Department official John Huang to testify on possible links between Clinton's aim of normalising U.S.-Vietnamese relations and improper foreign contributions to Clinton's election campaign.
Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott had made clear he believed the time had come for the Senate to vote on Peterson.

Smith dropped his objections to confirmation saying that Huang was out of the country and that he had received a letter from Clinton's national security adviser Sandy Berger, assuring him that Washington would continue pressing the Vietnamese for information about missing servicemen.
Peterson's nomination was strongly supported by Republican Sen. John McCain of Arizona, a former Navy pilot who was also held prisoner in Vietnam.
